focus: Packet map, process error (a) String.replace dollar-apostrophe, and the link-scan error class (b)
noveltyJustification: Six findings are new to this lineage: the (a) mechanism with its exact trigger string, the repo's existing replacer-function fix, the missing post-insertion shape check, the (b) link-scanner class with its three guards, the in-packet specimen, and the single-notation validator twin.
keyQuestions: Q1: What mechanism produced process error (a), where a helper's String.replace read a dollar-apostrophe sequence as a replacement pattern and pasted a tasks.md tail twice?

Q2: What mechanisms produced process errors (b) to (e): the validator parsing link-shaped task text, the reviewer wildcard rm, the committed regenerated scratch tree and the claims made before verification?
answeredQuestions: Q1: What mechanism produced process error (a), where a helper's String.replace read a dollar-apostrophe sequence as a replacement pattern and pasted a tasks.md tail twice?
ruledOut: A new repo-wide linter rejecting String.replace calls whose second argument is not a function - both known sites are already fixed and a scanner would have no failing caller today
Reproducing the (b) incident on a synthetic tasks.md - proves a class the shipped tests already pin, identifies no incident record

label: Process error (a) is the JavaScript replacement-pattern expansion of $': T050's check text ends '...It reports$' .skilled/...' and that string, passed as the string replacement argument of String.replace by the fix-unit insertion, expanded to the tasks.md tail and pasted it twice; the cause is recorded verbatim in the child goal log and the trigger survives in fix-chain.json and fix-units.json.

The same class already shipped to users once: the nested changelog generator read $' or $& in a user-authored summary as a replacement pattern and cut the summary short while pasting template text; the repo's fix (single-pass replacer function, durable comment) is the canonical pattern to copy for any text insertion, and a new linter for .replace call sites is rejected because both known sites are already fixed.

The insertion step had no post-insertion shape check: check-units.cjs proves each edit unit's OLD span occurs exactly once before the edit, but nothing compares the assembled tasks.md length before and after, so the doubled tail was caught by reading rather than by a check; the smallest fix is a line-count delta assertion inside the insertion helper itself.

Process error (b) is the link-scanner class: matchers must blank code spans and fences before resolving ]( text; three scanners in the current tree guard it (check-markdown-links.cjs blanks fences and spans with known-bad test rows; heal-spec-docs.cjs linkRepoint skips fenced lines and blanks spans; the validator anchor parser limits matching to non-code text). The incident-specific validator and run are not recorded anywhere in the packet, so the incident attribution stays UNKNOWN; the failing run's stderr or the pre-repair tasks.md would settle it.

The packet contains the exact byte shape (b) describes: 002/tasks.md:65 carries the backticked regex ["']([^"']+)["'] whose bytes include a close-bracket open-paren pair, which a scanner without code-span blanking reads as link text plus a link target; this is the in-packet specimen to keep as the regression fixture proving spans stay inert.

The same producing mechanism has a silent-pass twin in the validator: the goal binding row matcher now accepts bare text, a code span and a markdown link because recognising only one notation let the others pass a child that was never written; one matcher resolved link-shaped text as a link (a false positive) and the other failed to resolve a link-shaped binding (a false negative), both from hand-written prose parsed by a single-notation matcher.
